rules lens FAIL -> rework: Dominant strategy (rework): two placements build a deterministic, uncounterable win line. Place a white Gear 23 at mesh-distance 9 straight from the Drive Gear (13 black) down a column — quote: '13 (black) | ... | 9' in the Mesh Table for the 23 column — then a black Gear 13 at mesh-distance 9 further down the same column (row20→row11→row2), landing inside the 'within five holes of your edge' dial-read zone (§5d Re-dock). That final black 13 gives 1.00 'up' per crank, the fastest black rate in the numbers-per-turn table, and it accrues on every crank in the game, not just the owner's — quote: 'Thirty turns of the handle after that — everybody's turns, not just hers.' The Drive Gear 'may mesh several' (§5a), so every seat (N/S/E/W) can build the identical line off its own edge with zero contention, discoverable on a first read, with no Compound Hub ever touched. Sabotage does not deter it: a Pull costs the attacker one token plus a full turn (§5c) while gear_13 (8 copies) and gear_23 (5 copies) sit in open supply (bill), so the owner rebuilds next turn — a losing trade for the attacker. This makes the Compound Hub / Reading Ring subsystem, billed as 'the reason this game cannot be a deck of cards,' strategically optional filler.; idea.json contradiction (clarify): idea.json states 'First dial to 20 wins; a dial driven to -5 jams for one round,' but rules.md sets the win threshold at 30 (§4, §7) and makes a -5 dial lock permanently until the owner spends a full turn on Reset (§5e, §6) — both the win number and the penalty duration changed without the source concept being updated.; idea.json contradiction (clarify): idea.json's stated 'fun_correct_bet' is that direction flips on mesh-chain parity — 'your neighbour's mesh count goes odd' runs a dial backwards — but rules.md replaced that with a fixed rule independent of chain length: 'black climbs, white falls' (§1) and 'Every black gear ... turns clockwise. Every white gear ... turns anticlockwise. Always' (§5a). The parity-based tension the pitch was built on is absent from the shipped mechanic, which is consistent with the dominant straight-line route in the first finding.

killed (rework budget exhausted): rework budget exhausted: rules lens: R1 dominant-strategy/first-player-tempo: Setup step 6 docks in reverse turn order so the first player docks LAST, with full information on every other player's clamp, then also takes the first build+crank of the game. Evidence: "the last player in turn order clamps their Dial Unit first; the first player clamps last" and the stated rationale "the first player gets the first build and the first crank, so the last player gets first pick of the plate." This only balances tempo if picking last actually costs something, but the rules elsewhere say the plate has no real scarcity: "the gear supply (40) and the plate (6400 holes) are far larger than any count needs." With no scarcity, docking last is pure upside (best-informed pick, zero opportunity cost) stacked on top of moving first — the two advantages compound instead of offsetting, worst at 2p where one player sees the other's single clamp before choosing their own. Disposition: rework — reordering setup or adding real scarcity to docking is a mechanic change, not a wording fix.; R2 length-honesty: The rules' own pace estimate is already at the edge of plausible per-decision time, before accounting for the calculation load each placement actually requires. Evidence: "Expect 26 to 34 turns of the handle, at roughly a minute a turn including the placement hunt: 25 to 35 minutes." Each placement requires computing a mesh number (M = (teeth+teeth)/2), then hunting an 80x80 grid for a hole at exactly that straight-line or one-of-six-slant distance from an existing part, while also checking the foul zone (M to M+3) and loop/jam legality by hand. A full minute is plausible only if players have memorized the slant table; a first table is likely to run well past it. Disposition: rework — this is a property of the placement rule's search space, not fixable by rewording the estimate.; R3 clarify: Overview claims "You never add anything up. You crank, and the machine tells you what you built," which a cold reader will take as a blanket no-arithmetic promise, but §5a's core legality check is arithmetic every single turn: "M = (my teeth + their teeth) ÷ 2, counted in holes," plus counting distance d and mesh-count parity by hand. Disposition: clarify — narrow the claim to dial movement (which genuinely needs no addition) rather than the whole game.; R4 clarify: "dead gear" is used in §5a's meshing rule ("the Drive Gear counts, a hub end counts, a dead gear counts") before the document ever explains what a dead gear is — that only comes later in §5c ("Parts left with no live path back to the handle simply stop turning"). A first-time reader hits the term with nothing to resolve it against. Disposition: clarify — move or forward-reference the definition.

rules lens FAIL -> rework: Push orientation choice likely collapses to 'always head-first' (rework): pushing head-first (disc leading) never resolves worse than tail-first at the new joint — triggering a KICK always benefits the pusher (capture, or at worst a free reposition), and a CLAMP has no stated downside — while it ALSO leaves the uninformative bare tail exposed at the mouth. Tail-first only trades away this free upside to expose your own disc's polarity to future Probes and to a matching-pole kick from the next player at that mouth. Evidence: 'Choose which end goes in first: head first (disc leading, into the rail) or tail first (bare end leading, which leaves your disc facing out of the mouth).' The rules never show a concrete scenario where tail-first is correct, so a first-week player finds 'always head-first' and the game never punishes it.; Start-player draw has no termination guarantee (clarify): every player's 12 tiles are numbered 1-12 (bill: 'a number 1-12'), and setup step 6 lets each player freely pick which tile to stand up, with no random draw or simultaneous blind reveal required. Any player (or all of them) can keep showing their own '12' every round, forcing 'Re-do it if the highest is tied' indefinitely. Evidence: 'Each player stands one tile from their rack on the table, number up. Highest number goes first. Re-do it if the highest is tied.'
